ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a pedigree chart, circles represent females, squares represent males, and gray shading represents being affected. Individual 9 is the uncolored circle at the lower left, therefore is an unaffected female; she belongs to the same group of children as individuals 10, 11, and 12, and the parents are the gray square individual 3 on the left and the uncolored circle individual 4. The figure also shows that individual 7 is an affected male; his sons 13 and 14 with unaffected female 8 are unaffected, and daughter 15 is unaffected; individual 15 and unaffected male 16 have an affected son 18. Reasoning: The whole pedigree most conforms to X-linked recessive inheritance. An affected male can be produced by an unaffected mother; an affected father will not pass the X chromosome to sons, so the sons 13 and 14 of individual 7 are unaffected; but an affected father will pass the disease-carrying X to daughters, making daughter 15 able to become a carrier and give birth to affected son 18. Individual 12 is an affected female, which can also be explained by affected father 3 and carrier mother 4 jointly providing disease-carrying X. Therefore, according to this mode of inheritance, the genotype of individual 3 as an affected male is X^A Y, and he will pass X^A to all daughters. Individual 9 is the daughter of individual 3, so she must obtain X^A from her father; but individual 9 is uncolored and the question states complete penetrance, so she cannot be the affected female genotype X^A X^A. She can only obtain the normal allele X^a from mother 4, therefore the genotype of individual 9 is X^A X^a.

raw_record.question_text: The pedigree in the figure shows the mode of inheritance of a human disease that is associated with mutations in Gene A. method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify individual 9 as an unshaded female child of shaded male 3 and unshaded female 4. Infer the mode of inheritance from the whole pedigree as X-linked recessive because affected males occur from unaffected mothers, affected father 7 does not pass the disease to sons but his daughter 15 can have an affected son, and affected female 12 can arise from an affected father plus carrier mother. Then apply this to individual 9: father 3 must be X^A Y and passes X^A to every daughter. Since 9 is unshaded and penetrance is complete, she cannot be X^A X^A; therefore she must have received a normal X^a from mother 4. Conclude individual 9 is X^A X^a.
